h1: The 8 Best Lithium Jump Starters for Cars and Trucks, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Lithium Jump Starters 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 lithium jump starters scored on engine size limits, safety clamps, starts per charge, power bank use and cold tolerance.
summary: The NOCO Boost GB70 is the jump starter to buy if you drive a big V8, a diesel truck or an RV, because it is rated for engines up to 8.0L gas and 6.0L diesel. The NOCO Boost GB40 is the glove box pick for ordinary cars, the Type S DC10X adds a screen that walks you through the jump, and the AstroAI S8 is the lightest and cheapest way to carry a boost. Match the engine rating on the box to your vehicle before you look at any peak amp number.
intro: Peak amps are the number every jump starter box shouts, and it is the least useful number on the label. A pack claiming 6000A and a pack claiming 1000A can both fail to turn over the same cold diesel, because peak current lasts a fraction of a second and says nothing about how long the battery can keep the starter motor spinning. The figure that actually protects you is the engine size the maker lists, in liters of gas and diesel.

We ranked eight portable lithium packs on those engine ratings first, then on clamp safety, starts per charge, cold tolerance, weight and how well each doubles as a power bank. Every ranking comes from spec sheets, manuals and owner feedback, not bench work, so where a maker is vague about a rating we say so and mark the pack down.

products.name: NOCO Boost GB70 2000A UltraSafe Jump Starter, 12V Lithium Battery Booster
products.verdict: The only pack here rated for big gas V8s and 6.0L diesels, with the safest clamps in the group.
products.description:
The GB70 is rated at 2000 amps of peak current and lists engines up to 8.0L gas and 6.0L diesel, which is the largest gas rating after the two budget brands whose numbers we treat with caution. NOCO claims up to 40 starts per charge, a 400-lumen light with 7 modes, and an IP65 housing.

It ranks first because it pairs a believable engine rating with the UltraSafe clamp logic: spark-proof and reverse polarity protection mean a rushed connection in the dark does not arc. The GB40 below is lighter and cheaper, but it stops at 6.0L gas and 3.0L diesel, so a heavy-duty pickup is out of its range.

Buy it if you own a full-size truck, an RV or a boat with a big engine. The caveat is bulk: at 5 lb it is not a glove box item, and a full recharge takes about 6 hours.
products.idealFor: Owners of V8 trucks, diesels, RVs and boats who want one pack for everything.
products.skipIf: You drive a compact car and want something that fits a glove box.

products.name: NOCO Boost GB40 12V 1000A UltraSafe Portable Lithium Jump Starter
products.verdict: A 2.5 lb pack with the same safe clamps as its bigger sibling, sized for sedans and crossovers.
products.description:
The GB40 is the compact NOCO: 1000 amps of peak current, up to 20 starts per charge, a 100-lumen light with 7 modes, and the same UltraSafe protection against sparks and reversed clamps. It is rated for engines up to 6.0L gas and 3.0L diesel, and the whole pack weighs 2.5 lb.

It sits one place below the GB70 for a plain reason: range. Half the weight and half the starts mean it suits four-cylinder and V6 cars comfortably, but a 6.0L diesel pickup is beyond its rating. Against the Type S DC10X it gives up the screen and wireless charging, yet it recharges in about 3 hours and carries an IP65 rating the Type S lacks.

It is the right buy for commuters and families with one or two ordinary cars. The caveat is the 1-year warranty and a 3.0L diesel ceiling that rules out most heavy trucks.
products.idealFor: Drivers of sedans, crossovers and small SUVs who want a dependable glove box pack.
products.skipIf: You tow, drive a diesel pickup or need more than 20 starts between charges.

products.name: TYPE S DC10X 1000A Car Jump Starter, Wireless Charging Power Bank, 8000mAh
products.verdict: An LCD that talks you through each step, plus a 10W wireless charging pad on top.
products.description:
The DC10X is the beginner's pack. An LCD shows battery percentage and a three-step prompt (clamp, start, unplug), the smart cable warns on reverse polarity, and the 8000mAh power bank includes a 10W wireless pad. It is rated for 6.0L gas and 4.0L diesel and weighs 2.2 lb.

It lands behind the NOCO packs because its specification wording is more careful than most and, honestly, more telling: the maker states 500A of cranking current for 0.3 seconds and 1000A peak for 0.1 seconds. Those are modest sustained numbers, so we weight the NOCO engine ratings higher. It beats the DL20 below on diesel capacity, 4.0L against 3.0L.

Buy it for a household where a nervous driver may need to use it alone at night. The caveat is a 1-year warranty and a splash-resistant, not sealed, shell.
pros: LCD walks you through the jump
products.idealFor: New drivers and shared family cars where clear on-screen steps matter.
products.skipIf: You want a sealed housing or an engine rating above 6.0L gas.

products.name: Type S Dynamic Light DL20 1000A Car Battery Jump Starter 12V 6L Gas 3L Diesel
products.verdict: The DC10X's smarter-cable system with a bigger 10,000mAh battery, but a lower diesel rating.
products.description:
The DL20 shares the JumpGuide screen and the spark-proof, overheat-protected Safe and Smart cables of the DC10X, but swaps the wireless pad for a 10,000mAh bank with USB-C input and output. It is rated at 1,000 amps max for 6L gas and 3L diesel engines, and it carries emergency hazard lights.

It ranks a step under the DC10X because the engine ceiling drops from 4.0L to 3L diesel and the maker gives no weight or cold-temperature figure to weigh against. The extra battery capacity is real, though, and USB-C recharging is quick compared with older micro-USB packs.

Pick it if you also want a roadside phone and tablet charger and drive petrol cars. The caveat is that the listing is thin on durability detail, so treat the housing as a daily-carry, not a work-site, pack.
products.idealFor: Commuters who want one device for jump starts and phone top-ups.
products.skipIf: You drive a diesel truck or want a published low-temperature spec.

products.award: Best for Large Engines on a Budget
products.name: S ZEVZO ET03 Car Jump Starter 4000A for Up to 8.0L Gas and 7.0L Diesel Engines
products.verdict: Big-engine claims and a force-start button at a mid-range price, with numbers we read cautiously.
products.description:
The ET03 claims 4000 amps of peak current, support for engines up to 8.0L gas and 7.0L diesel, and up to 50 jump starts per charge from a 74Wh battery. A force-start function in the clamps targets batteries at 0V, and a 500-lumen light has stable, strobe and SOS modes. Working range is 14F to 140F.

It ranks below the NOCO GB70 because peak-amp claims at this level are hard to compare across brands, while the GB70 gives a conservative 2000A with a similar engine range. The ET03 does offer a 7.0L diesel rating that exceeds the NOCO's 6.0L and costs less, which is why it still places fifth.

Buy it for a heavy truck on a budget. The caveat is that the maker advises charging to above 14V before using it on a dead battery, and the 14F lower limit makes it a poor deep-winter choice.
cons: Peak figure is hard to verify
Needs a full charge for dead batteries
products.idealFor: Owners of heavy trucks and boats who want big-engine ratings at a lower cost.
products.skipIf: You live somewhere that regularly drops below 14F.

products.name: OXILAM Jump Starter 6000A for All Gas/12L Diesel, Lithium Jump Box with Jumper Cables
products.verdict: The largest claimed ratings on the page, which is exactly why they need a pinch of salt.
products.description:
The OXILAM lists 6000A peak, all gas engines and diesels to 12L, up to 60 jump starts per charge, ten safety protections, an 800-lumen three-mode light and a Type-C input. It has a protective cover and a non-slip side grip.

It ranks sixth because a 12L diesel rating and a 6000A peak describe a pack that is physically very small for those figures, and the NOCO GB70 at 5 lb lists a more modest 2000A. We keep the OXILAM on the list for its feature count and its 60-start claim, but we do not rank claims we cannot reconcile above ones we can.

It is a fine pick for light vehicles, lawn tractors and a spare in a work truck. Keep it above 50 percent charge before a jump and top it up every three months in storage, as the maker itself advises.
products.idealFor: Anyone starting multiple small engines, such as mowers, ATVs and a family car.
products.skipIf: You are buying specifically for a large diesel and want a rating you can trust.

products.name: AstroAI S8 Car Battery Jump Starter 1500A, Portable 12V Lithium Jump Box
products.verdict: At 0.95 lb it is the lightest pack here and the cheapest, with a boost button for flat batteries.
products.description:
The S8 weighs 0.95 lb, measures 7.9 by 4.5 by 3.7 inches, and lists 1500A peak from a 45C high-rate battery for engines up to 6.0L gas and 3.0L diesel. Auto-Sense lights a green LED when a battery reads under 9V and needs the boost button. A three-mode light and basic power bank sit alongside.

It ranks seventh because its smart cables are less thoroughly described than NOCO's, and there is no screen or published water rating. It is the cheapest pack here, in the $30 to $50 bracket, and the lightest, which matters if the pack lives in a motorcycle seat or a hatch pocket.

Buy it as a backup for a small car. The caveat is a 3.0L diesel limit and little documentation of cold performance.
products.idealFor: Drivers of small cars who want the lightest, lowest-cost safety net.
products.skipIf: You want a screen, an IP rating or diesel truck capacity.

products.award: Best for Compact Power Bank Use
products.name: Type S Dynamic Classic DC10 Car Battery Jump Starter Portable Power Bank 500A
products.verdict: The most modest starter in the list, with the best-documented USB charging output.
products.description:
The DC10 gives 550A of peak current for gas engines to 6.0L and diesels to 4.0L, a USB-C port (up to 20V at 3.25A) and a USB-A port, and a safety suite covering reverse polarity, overcurrent, overvoltage, overload and short circuit. It works from -4F to 93F.

It ranks last because 550A of peak current is the lowest here, and the listing names no screen or light. Against the DL20 it trades a smaller sustained claim for a similar engine range, so it works best as a compact backup rather than a primary pack. The cold range is honest, though, which many rivals do not publish.

Buy it if you want a small pack that doubles as a competent USB-C charger. The caveat is limited headroom on a cold morning with a big engine.
products.idealFor: Small-car owners who value a tidy charger and an emergency boost in one.
products.skipIf: You want headroom for a cold start on a larger engine.

whatMatters.detail: Makers publish a maximum engine displacement in liters, split into gas and diesel. Diesel is lower because compression is higher and the starter draws more. Ignore the peak amp headline and find your engine on the listing: a 5.0L V8 gas needs a pack rated to at least 6.0L gas, and a 3.0L diesel wants a rating above that.

Peak amps are a brief surge, often measured for a fraction of a second. Cranking amps describe what the pack can sustain while the engine turns over. Type S, for example, openly lists 500A cranking next to 1000A peak. When a listing gives only a huge peak figure and nothing else, treat it as marketing.

Cheap clamps can arc if they touch the wrong terminal. Look for words such as spark-proof, reverse polarity protection and overheat protection, and prefer a pack where the cable signals an error with a light or beep. This matters most at night, in rain or when a nervous driver is doing the connecting.

Lithium cells lose output in the cold and may refuse to discharge below a set temperature. Only some listings publish a range: the Type S DC10 runs from -4F, the S ZEVZO ET03 from 14F. If you live where winters bite, favor a pack with a printed low-temperature limit and keep it indoors until needed.

A lithium pack self-discharges and degrades if left empty. The OXILAM maker suggests recharging every three months, and wants above 50 percent charge before a jump. Check the listing for recharge time, standby guidance and whether the pack can handle the heat inside a parked car.

faq.q: Will a 1000A jump starter start my truck?
faq.a: It depends on the engine, not the amps. The NOCO Boost GB40 is rated to 6.0L gas but only 3.0L diesel, so a 6.7L diesel pickup needs the NOCO Boost GB70 or the S ZEVZO ET03.

faq.q: Is it safe to connect the clamps in the wrong order?
faq.a: Packs such as the NOCO GB70 and the TYPE S DC10X include reverse polarity protection that blocks power if the clamps are reversed. Always follow the manual order anyway, and do not trust cheap packs without a stated protection.

faq.q: Is the OXILAM 6000A really better than a 2000A NOCO?
faq.a: Not by a margin you can rely on. Peak current is a brief figure, and the OXILAM reaches it from a far smaller body than the NOCO GB70. Choose by the engine rating and clamp safety.

faq.q: How do I use one on a completely flat battery?
faq.a: Use the boost or force-start button, as on the AstroAI S8 or S ZEVZO ET03, after the pack is fully charged. The ET03 maker advises charging above 14V first. If the engine still does not turn, stop and call roadside help.

faq.q: How often should I recharge the pack?
faq.a: Top it up every three months, as OXILAM recommends, and keep it above 50 percent. The NOCO GB40 recharges in about 3 hours, the GB70 in about 6, so schedule it. Do not store a lithium pack empty.

faq.q: Can I leave it in the car in summer or winter?
faq.a: Heat and cold both shorten lithium life. The Type S DC10 lists -4F to 93F and the ET03 14F to 140F, so a car cabin can exceed those limits. Keep the pack in a cooler spot in extreme weather if possible.

finalTake: Buy the NOCO Boost GB70 if you drive a truck, a diesel or an RV, and the NOCO Boost GB40 if your needs are an ordinary car and a glove box. The TYPE S DC10X is the right pick if the person using it is nervous and wants on-screen guidance. Treat any pack that promises thousands of amps and a 12L diesel rating with suspicion, and always check the engine size line before you check the price.
